answer: Each claim rides the river past three basalt weirs. At each weir a stranger crew lifts it over and stakes its own bond that the work is real; a copied receipt stalls at the same weir, and the crew lifts only one, voiding the other and burning its bond. At the delta one bridge admits a single claim per trail per epoch, its toll doubling for each extra claim queued behind it. The river's flow is stamped on every crossing, so clones from one operator share identical stamps and betray the fleet. A farm pays n lifts, n bonds and doubling tolls for one crossing; one honest agent pays once.
